title: Physical change
competency: Describe physical change with everyday examples.

keywords.def: A change in physical appearance, not in chemical composition. No new substance forms.

en.text: A physical change changes how a substance looks, but not what it is made of. No new substance forms. Melting ice, grinding salt, tearing paper, making an iron bar magnetic, evaporating water, dissolving sugar and breaking a stick are physical changes.

screens.title: Torn paper
screens.ask: You tear a sheet of paper into small pieces. Is each piece still paper?
opts: No, it is a new substance
screens.after:
Yes. Each small piece is still paper.
Only the size and shape changed. No new substance formed.
This is a physical change.

screens.title: 2.4 Change around us
paras: Change is happening around us all the time.
Changes are classified as physical or chemical changes.

screens.title: 2.4.1 Physical change
paras: A physical change changes the physical appearance of a substance.
It does not change the chemical composition.
A new substance is never formed.

screens.title: Common physical changes
items: Solid water becomes liquid water. Still water.
Big crystals become powder. Still salt.
The sugar is still there; evaporate the water to get it back.
Smaller pieces of the same wood.

screens.title: What changed: size and shape, or state?
screens.text: In each physical change, sort what changed.
items: Small pieces of the same paper.
Big crystals become fine powder. Still salt.
Smaller pieces of the same wood.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A change in physical appearance, not in chemical composition. No new substance forms.

screens.text: Which of these is a physical change?
screens.why:
A physical change forms no new substance.
When water evaporates, the vapour is still water. It condenses back to liquid.
Burning charcoal, rusting and food spoilage all form new substances: chemical changes.
So evaporation of water is the physical change.
screens.clue: Which one forms no new substance?

screens.text: True or false? A new substance forms in a physical change.
screens.why:
A physical change alters only the appearance: size, shape or state.
The chemical composition stays the same.
A new substance is never formed. So the statement is false.

screens.text: Name the kind of change: a change in size, shape and state of a substance is a …
screens.why:
Size, shape and state are physical properties.
Changing them does not change what the substance is made of.
Example: ice melting is still water.
So it is a physical change.
screens.clue: Does the substance stay the same?

screens.text: Which one of these is a physical change?
screens.why:
Making an iron bar magnetic: the iron stays iron. Nothing new forms. Physical.
Burning a candle forms carbon dioxide and water vapour: chemical.
Fermentation forms alcohol and carbon dioxide: chemical.
So "All of them" is wrong. The answer is making an iron bar magnetic.
screens.clue: Which one leaves the substance unchanged?

test.text: Classify the change: melting of ice is a …
test.why:
Melting turns solid ice into liquid water.
It is still water: only the state changed.
So melting is a physical change.

test.text: True or false? Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change.
test.why:
The sugar spreads through the water, but it is still sugar.
Evaporate the water and the sugar is left again.
No new substance forms, so it is a physical change. True.

test.text: Find the odd one out: which is NOT a physical change?
test.why:
Tearing paper, grinding salt and breaking a stick change only size or shape.
Burning wood makes ash, smoke and gases: new substances.
So burning wood is a chemical change, not a physical one.

test.ask: Complete the definition: in a physical change, no new ___ is formed.
test.why:
A physical change alters size, shape or state.
The chemical composition does not change.
So no new substance is formed.

test.text: Two changes in a row: Abebe melts butter, then lets it cool and harden again. Which is true?
opts: The butter becomes a new substance
test.why:
Melting: solid butter → liquid butter. Only the state changes.
Cooling: liquid butter → solid butter. Only the state changes again.
It is still butter, so no new substance formed.
Both steps are physical changes.
